#hri #robot 

>**Braitenberg vehicles** are ==a set of thought experiments introduced by neuroscientist Valentino Braitenberg in his 1984 book, _[Vehicles: Experiments in Synthetic Psychology](https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262521123/vehicles/)_==. These hypothetical machines demonstrate how complex, seemingly intelligent behaviors—like "love," "fear," or "aggression"—can emerge from extremely simple mechanical designs.

>Core Concept
>The vehicles are built using just three basic components: **sensors** (to detect stimuli like light or heat), **motors** (to drive wheels), and **wires** that connect them. Braitenberg uses these to illustrate the "Law of Uphill Analysis and Downhill Invention," suggesting it is much easier to build a simple machine that looks complex than it is to analyze a complex machine and find its simple rules. ![YouTube](data:image/png;base64,)YouTube +3
>Key Vehicle Types and Behaviors
Braitenberg described 14 different vehicles, each adding a layer of complexity. Here are the foundational models: ![Sarah Lawrence College](https://encrypted-tbn3.gstatic.com/faviconV2?url=https://science.slc.edu&client=AIM&size=128&type=FAVICON&fallback_opts=TYPE,SIZE,URL)Sarah Lawrence College
- **Vehicle 1: Getting Around.** One sensor connected to one motor. The more stimulus (e.g., heat), the faster the motor goes. It appears to "dislike" heat because it rushes through hot areas and lingers in cold ones.
- **Vehicle 2: Fear and Aggression.** Two sensors and two motors with "excitatory" (direct) connections.
    - **2a (Fear/Cowardice):** Sensors connect to the motor on the same side. If light is on the right, the right wheel spins faster, turning the vehicle away from the light.
    - **2b (Aggression):** Sensors cross-connect (left sensor to right motor). It turns toward the light and charges it at high speed.
- **Vehicle 3: Love and Exploration.** Two sensors and two motors with "inhibitory" connections (more light makes the motor go slower).
    - **3a (Love):** Sensors connect to motors on the same side. It turns toward the light and slows to a stop right in front of it, seemingly "basking" in its presence.
    - **3b (Exploration):** Sensors cross-connect. It turns toward a light but then speeds away toward the next one, appearing "curious" or "restless".
- **Vehicle 4: Values and Special Tastes.** Introduces non-linear connections where the motor might only respond to a specific range of intensity, giving the vehicle "preferences" for certain environments. ![Wikipedia](data:image/png;base64,)Wikipedia +5
